title: Consider the inputs.
text: For which of these functions can you plug in a value like $$x=100?$$

title: The range of the trig function is the domain of its inverse
text: Recall the relationship between the range of a trig function and the domain of its inverse. The range of $$\tan(x)$$ is $$(-\infty,\infty).$$\n##figure1.gif##

figureAlts.figure1.gif: Graph of the trigonometric function x equals tangent of theta on a coordinate plane with a faint grid. The horizontal axis is theta, and the vertical axis is x. The curve is strictly increasing and passes directly through the origin. It is bounded by two vertical dashed lines representing asymptotes: a left asymptote at theta equals negative pi over two; and a right asymptote at theta equals pi over two.

title: The range of the trig function is the domain of its inverse
text: While the domains of $$\arcsin(x)$$ and $$\arccos(x)$$ are the bounded interval $$[-1,1],$$ $$\arctan(x)$$ is defined for all real numbers.\n##figure2.gif##

figureAlts.figure2.gif: Graph of the inverse trigonometric function theta equals arctangent of x. The horizontal axis is x, and the vertical axis is theta. The curve is strictly increasing for all real numbers, passing through the origin. It approaches, but never touches, two horizontal dashed lines representing asymptotes at theta equals pi over two, and theta equals negative pi over two.
